title.narrative: Security of the building and access to the documentary heritage of the Damascus Museum

description.narrative: Established in the 20th century, the National Museum of Damascus preserves collections from Palmyra, Bosra, Aleppo, the Euphrates valley and other major sites; many objects were relocated there during the conflict. The museum faces conflict-related threats, illicit trafficking risks, infrastructure degradation and resource constraints. Security is partly outdated and fragmented, with aging CCTV, limited intrusion detection, uneven perimeter control and coverage gaps. UNESCO is upgrading select security and fire-prevention equipment, reorganizing storage, assessing documentary heritage, improving documentation and delivering initial emergency-response training. Full protection requires multilayer security, contingency planning and sustained capacity-building.
